Rashi on Yevamot 11a:10:1.english: Like those with whom relations are forbidden - For it is written: “Do not defile yourselves in any of these” (Leviticus 18:24).

Rashi on Yevamot 11a:11:1.hebrew: ביאתה או חליצתה וכו' - האשה שהלך בעלה למדינת הים, ובאו ואמרו לה: מת בעליך, ונשאת, ואח"כ בא בעלה — תצא מזה ומזה. מתו, אחיו של זה ואחיו של זה חולצין ולא מייבמין. רבי שמעון אומר: ביאתה או חליצתה מאחיו של ראשון — פוטרת היא לכתחלה את צרתה, שהרי היא כשאר נשים לגבי יבם, דלא קנסוה רבנן מיבם, דודאי שריא ליה, שאנוסה היתה ששמעה שמת. אלמא, נבעלה תחת בעלה — שריא צרתה לייבם, ואפי' רבנן לא פליגי אר"ש אלא בדידה, אבל בצרתה מודו:
Rashi on Yevamot 11a:11:1.english: Her relations or her ḥalitza, etc. - [The Mishnah states:] A woman whose husband went overseas, and [people] came and told her, "Your husband died," and she married [another man], and afterward her husband came [back] — she must leave both this one and that one. [If they] died, the brothers of this one and the brothers of that one perform ḥalitza and may not perform levirate marriage. Rabbi Shimon says: Her relations or her ḥalitza from the brother of the first [husband] exempts her rival wife in the first instance, for she is like all other women with respect to the levir, as the Rabbis did not penalize her [by barring her] from the levir — for she is certainly permitted to him, since she acted under unavoidable circumstances, having heard that [he] had died. Thus, [when a woman] had relations [with another man] while under her husband, her rival wife is permitted to be taken in levirate marriage, and even the Rabbis disagree with Rabbi Shimon only regarding her herself, whereas regarding her rival wife they agree.

Rashi on Yevamot 11a:12:1.english: A sotah by Torah law - [A woman] who committed adultery, and the Torah forbade her [to her husband].

Rashi on Yevamot 11a:12:2.hebrew: ואת אמרת לי סוטה דרבנן - דהא מדאורייתא שריא, שניסת ע"פ ב"ד בעד אחד ואנוסה היא, ורחמנא שריא, דכתיב (במדבר ה): "ועד אין בה" — תרי, אלא אחד; "והיא לא נתפסה" — אסורה, הא נתפסה — מותרת. ורבנן הוא דגזרו בה, כי היכי דתידוק שפיר שמת בעלה עד שלא תנשא:
Rashi on Yevamot 11a:12:2.english: And you speak to me [of] a sota by rabbinic [law] - For by Torah law she is permitted, as she married by [authorization of] the court on [the testimony of] one witness and she is [considered] forced, and the Merciful One permitted [her], as it is written (Numbers 5[:13]): "And there is no witness against her" — [meaning not] two [witnesses], rather one; "and she was not seized" — [then] she is forbidden, [implying that] if she was seized, she is permitted. Rather, it is the Rabbis who decreed [a prohibition] upon her, so that she would investigate thoroughly that her husband died before she marries.

Rashi on Yevamot 11a:13:1.hebrew: ודקארי לה מאי קארי לה - הא לא אמר רב אלא בסוטה דאורייתא, דכתיב בה טומאה:
Rashi on Yevamot 11a:13:1.english: And he who asked it, why did he ask it? - Surely, Rav only stated [his ruling] regarding a sotah by Torah law, concerning whom "defilement" is written.

Rashi on Yevamot 11a:13:2.hebrew: קסבר - האי דפריך, כל דתקון רבנן כעין דאורייתא תקון. ואי סוטה דאורייתא היא וצרתה אסורה, הכי נמי הוו אסרי רבנן צרה מייבום ומצרכי לה חליצה:
Rashi on Yevamot 11a:13:2.english: He held - This one who raised the objection [held that] whatever the Sages instituted, they instituted parallel to Torah [law]; and if it is a sotah by Torah [law] and her rival wife is forbidden, so too the Sages would forbid the rival wife from levirate marriage and require chalitzah for her.

Rashi on Yevamot 11a:14:1.english: She entered with him - [This refers to] one who expresses jealousy to his wife and said to her, "Do not be secluded with so-and-so."

Rashi on Yevamot 11a:14:2.hebrew: לביתה - לבעלה, שמא זינתה, שרגלים לדבר, שהרי קינא לה ונסתרה. ואם כהנת היא, אסורה בתרומה, כדיליף במסכת סוטה (דף כח.): "נטמאה", "נטמאה", "ונטמאה" — ג' פעמים: אחד לבעל, ואחד לבועל, ואחד לתרומה:
Rashi on Yevamot 11a:14:2.english: To her house - To her husband, lest she committed adultery, as there are grounds for the matter, for he had warned her and she secluded herself [with that man]. And if she is [the wife of] a priest, she is forbidden [to partake] of teruma, as [the Gemara] derives in Tractate Sotah (28a): "she was defiled," "she was defiled," "and she was defiled" — three times: one [forbids her] to [her] husband, and one to the adulterer, and one to teruma.

Rashi on Yevamot 11a:1:1.english: [It] is difficult - For Rav Sheshet, who answered it thus.

Rashi on Yevamot 11a:1:2.hebrew: רב אשי סבר לה כריש לקיש - דאמר בכרת, וסיפא ניחא:
Rashi on Yevamot 11a:1:2.english: Rav Ashi holds in accordance with Reish Lakish - Who said [that it involves] karet, and [thus] the latter clause is resolved.

Rashi on Yevamot 11a:1:3.hebrew: ומתרץ לה - לרישא דברייתא דקתני "צריך חליצה", באחים שנולדו לאחר חליצה וקדושין של שני, וכר' שמעון דאמר "ייבם ולבסוף נולד", לא מהניא נפילתה מן הראשון למהוי עלה אשת אחיו שלא היה בעולמו. הלכך, זיקת ההיא נפילה לא אסרה לה עליה דהאי, הואיל וכשנולד כבר קדשה זה:
Rashi on Yevamot 11a:1:3.english: And [he] resolves it - [Namely,] the first clause of the baraita, which teaches [that she] requires chalitzah — [this refers] to brothers who were born after the chalitzah and betrothal of the second [brother], and [this is] in accordance with Rabbi Shimon, who says [that when one] performed yibbum and afterwards [a brother] was born, her falling [into levirate eligibility] from the first [brother] does not take effect to make her [forbidden] to him [as] the wife of his brother who was not in his world. Therefore, the zikah [levirate bond] of that falling does not forbid her to this [brother], since when he was born, this [second brother] had already betrothed her.

Rashi on Yevamot 11a:1:4.hebrew: רבינא סבר לה כרבי יוחנן - דאמר חייבי לאוין נינהו, ורישא ניחא. ומתרץ לסיפא, דקתני "אין לה עליו כלום", באחין שנולדו לאחר מכאן, וכרבנן דאמרי אשת אחיו שלא היה בעולמו היא, ולא תקשי רישא לסיפא:
Rashi on Yevamot 11a:1:4.english: Ravina holds in accordance with Rabbi Yochanan - Who said [that] they are [subject to] negative prohibitions, and [thus] the first clause is resolved. And he resolves the latter clause, which teaches, "She has no [claim] upon him at all," [as referring] to brothers who were born afterward, and in accordance with the Rabbis, who say she is the wife of his brother who was not in his world [i.e., alive during his lifetime], so that the first clause does not contradict the latter clause.

Rashi on Yevamot 11a:3:1.hebrew: הילודים - שנולדו אחר קדושין של זה, ולא איתסרא עלייהו בחליצתו, דהא זיקה קמייתא לא רמאי קמייהו לייבומי, ומשום אשת אחיו שלא היה בעולמו לא מיתסרא, כר"ש, דאמר: ייבם ולבסוף נולד — שריא:
Rashi on Yevamot 11a:3:1.english: The newborn [brothers] - [Those] who were born after this [brother]'s betrothal [of her], and she did not become forbidden to them through his ḥalitzah, for the first levirate bond was not cast before them for levirate marriage; and on account of [the prohibition of] the wife of his brother who was not in his world, she is not forbidden, in accordance with Rabbi Shimon, who says [that if a brother] performed levirate marriage and afterward [another brother] was born, she is permitted.

Rashi on Yevamot 11a:4:1.english: One of those who were born arose - [Those] who were [alive] at the time of the first chalitzah.

Rashi on Yevamot 11a:4:2.hebrew: אין לה עליו כלום - כר"ל, דאמר האחין חייבין על החלוצה כרת:
Rashi on Yevamot 11a:4:2.english: She has nothing against him - In accordance with Reish Lakish, who says [that] the brothers are liable to karet for [cohabiting with] a chalutzah.

Rashi on Yevamot 11a:6:1.hebrew: עמד אחד מן הילודים - אחר חליצה או אפילו אחר קדושין, וכשמת זה החולץ קדשה אותו ילוד, אין לה עליו כלום. ולאו משום חליצה, אלא משום דהויא אשת אחיו שלא היה בעולמו מנפילה ראשונה:
Rashi on Yevamot 11a:6:1.english: One of the newborn [brothers] arose - after chalitzah or even after betrothal, and when this one who performed chalitzah died, that newborn [brother] betrothed her, she has no [claim] on him. And [this is] not because of chalitzah, rather because she is the wife of his brother who was not in his world from the first falling [to levirate marriage].

Rashi on Yevamot 11a:6:2.english: In accordance with whom? In accordance with the Rabbis - Who say [that] even [if] he performed levirate marriage [with her] and afterward [the other brother] was born, she is forbidden [to him].

Rashi on Yevamot 11a:7:1.hebrew: בעשה - בית אחד הוא בונה ואין בונה ב' בתים, ולאו הבא מכלל עשה, עשה:
Rashi on Yevamot 11a:7:1.english: [In violation] of a positive mitzva - He builds one house, and does not build two houses; and a prohibition derived from a positive mitzva [has the status of] a positive mitzva.

Rashi on Yevamot 11a:8:1.hebrew: ומ"ד בכרת כר"ל - דאמר לאו שליחות דאחים קעביד, הלכך הוא ניהו דקאי עלה בעשה, אבל אחים כדקיימי קיימי באיסור אשת אח:
Rashi on Yevamot 11a:8:1.english: And the one who said [that it is] by karet [holds] like Reish Lakish - Who said he does not perform the agency of the brothers; therefore, it is he who stands under a positive commandment regarding her, whereas the brothers remain as they stood, under the prohibition of a brother's wife.

Rashi on Yevamot 11a:8:2.hebrew: מ"ד בעשה כרבי יוחנן - דאמר איהו שליחותא דאחין קעביד, וכי היכי דלדידיה הויא צרה בעשה, לאחים נמי הויא בעשה:
Rashi on Yevamot 11a:8:2.english: The one who says [it is] a positive commandment [holds] in accordance with Rabbi Yochanan - For he says [that] he acts as the agent of the brothers, and just as for him the rival wife is [prohibited by] a positive commandment, for the brothers as well she is [prohibited by] a positive commandment.

Rashi on Yevamot 11a:9:1.hebrew: צרת סוטה אסורה - היה נשוי ב' נשים, וזינתה האחת תחתיו ויש עדים, ומת בלא בנים — היא וצרתה פטורות אף מן החליצה. מאי טעמא? טומאה כתיב בה: ונסתרה והיא נטמאה (במדבר ה׳:י״ג):
Rashi on Yevamot 11a:9:1.english: The rival wife of a sotah is forbidden - [If a man] was married to two women, and one [of them] committed adultery while married to him and there are witnesses, and he died without children — she and her rival wife are exempt even from chalitzah. What is the reason? [Because] defilement is written regarding her: "and she was secluded and she was defiled" (Numbers 5:13).

Tosafot on Yevamot 11a:11:1.hebrew: רבי שמעון אומר ביאתה או חליצתה כו' - וא"ת, ואמאי לא מקשה מת"ק דאמר: אחיו של זה ואחיו של זה חולצין, ולרב לא בעינן חליצה? וי"ל, דהא אתי ליה שפיר דחולצת, דמדאורייתא בעיא חליצה, דסוטה דרבנן היא; ולא פריך מר' שמעון אלא משום דכל דתקון רבנן כעין דאורייתא תקון, והיה לנו לאוסרה להתייבם. וא"ת, ודלמא ר' שמעון לא קאמר אלא דבדיעבד פוטרת צרתה, אבל לכתחלה לא? ואמר ר"י דבדיעבד מודה ת"ק, דלא אשכחן דפליגי. והא דלא נקט: אחיו של ראשון רצה חולץ רצה מייבם, דמשמע לכתחלה — אמר ר"י דמילתא אגב אורחיה קמ"ל, דאע"ג דאיכא צרה דשייך בה ייבום טפי, אפ"ה ביאתה או חליצה שלה פוטרת לכתחילה צרתה, דס"ד דלא פטרה, דנראה כאשתו דשני. וא"ת, לרב חסדא שרוצה לדקדק דסוטה דאורייתא שריא, תקשי ליה מתני' דפרק קמא דסוטה (דף ב. ודף ו. ושם) דמייתי בסמוך, דספק סוטה אינה מתייבמת? וי"ל, דהוה אמינא דהא דקתני שאין מתייבמת היינו מדרבנן; אע"ג דהתם מוכח דאסירא מדאורייתא, מכל מקום מכח משנה עצמה אין להוכיח עליו כלום. ועוד אמר רבי יצחק, דדוקא לרב פריך, דמשוי ליה כערוה לסוטה דאורייתא ופטורה אף מן החליצה, ולכך בסוטה דרבנן סברא היא דיש לאוסרה להתייבם; אבל בההיא דסוטה, דספק סוטה חולצת, אין תימה אם נאמר דבסוטה דרבנן אפילו מתייבמת. ועוד פירש רבינו יצחק, דלרבי שמעון אסורה להתייבם לכתחלה, מדקתני סיפא: "ואין הולד ממזר" — דאי שרי לייבם לכתחלה, פשיטא דאין הולד ממזר! ועוד, בירושלמי קורא לההיא דרבי שמעון "חליצה פסולה", ואם היתה מותרת להתייבם, חליצה כשרה היא. ופריך מהא דקאמר ר"ש דפוטרת צרתה, דכיון דאמר בסוטה דאורייתא דלאו בת חליצה וייבום היא, בסוטה דרבנן אין לחליצה להועיל לפטור צרתה. וכ"ת: ממה נפשך תועיל, דאם חשיבא כסוטה גמורה, צרתה נמי לא בעי חליצה, ואי לא חשיבא כסוטה, א"כ שפיר פטרה צרתה? יש לומר דמסתבר ליה להש"ס דכיון דדמיא לסוטה דאורייתא, חליצתה כמאן דליתא ואין לה לפטור צרתה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 11a:11:1.english: Rabbi Shimon says: Her relations or her ḥalitza, etc. - And if you ask: Why does he [Rav Ḥisda] not raise an objection from the first Tanna, who says [that] the brother of this one and the brother of that one perform ḥalitza, whereas according to Rav we do not require ḥalitza [for a sota]? And one can answer that this works out well for him [Rav] that she performs ḥalitza, because by Torah law she requires ḥalitza, as this [woman who remarried] is [only] a rabbinic sota; and he [Rav Ḥisda] only objects from Rabbi Shimon because whatever the Sages instituted, they instituted in the manner of Torah law, so we should have forbidden her from entering into levirate marriage. And if you ask: Perhaps Rabbi Shimon only said that after the fact [bedi'avad] she exempts her rival wife, but ab initio [lekhateḥila] she may not [do so]? And R. Yitzḥak says that after the fact, the first Tanna agrees [that she exempts her rival wife], for we do not find that they disagree [on that]. And as for why he [Rabbi Shimon] did not state: "The brother of the first [husband] may, if he wishes, perform ḥalitza, or if he wishes, perform levirate marriage," which would imply ab initio — R. Yitzḥak says that he teaches us something incidentally: that even though there is a rival wife to whom levirate marriage is more applicable, nevertheless her relations or her ḥalitza exempts her rival wife ab initio; for you might have thought that she does not exempt [her], since she appears like the wife of the second [husband]. And if you ask: According to Rav Ḥisda, who seeks to infer that a biblical sota is permitted [to the yavam], let the Mishnah in the first chapter of Sota (2a and 6a, and there [in that chapter]), which [the Gemara] cites shortly, pose a difficulty for him, [as it teaches] that an uncertain sota may not enter into levirate marriage! And one can answer that he would say that what it teaches — that she may not enter into levirate marriage — is by rabbinic law; even though there [in Sota] it is proven that she is forbidden by Torah law, nevertheless from the Mishnah itself nothing can be proven against him. Furthermore, Rabbi Yitzḥak said that he [Rav Ḥisda] specifically objects against Rav, who treats a biblical sota like an erva [a forbidden relative] so that she is exempt even from ḥalitza, and therefore in the case of a rabbinic sota it is logical that she should be forbidden from entering into levirate marriage; however, regarding that [Mishnah] in Sota, where an uncertain sota performs ḥalitza, it is no wonder if we say that in the case of a rabbinic sota she may even enter into levirate marriage. Furthermore, Rabbeinu Yitzḥak explained that according to Rabbi Shimon she is forbidden from entering into levirate marriage ab initio, from what the latter clause [of the Mishnah] teaches: "and the child is not a mamzer" — for if it were permitted to perform levirate marriage ab initio, it would be obvious that the child is not a mamzer! Moreover, in the [Talmud] Yerushalmi it calls that [ḥalitza] of Rabbi Shimon an "invalid ḥalitza," whereas if she were permitted to enter into levirate marriage, it would be a valid ḥalitza. And he [Rav Ḥisda] objects from this that Rabbi Shimon says that she exempts her rival wife: since he [Rav] says regarding a biblical sota that she is not subject to ḥalitza or levirate marriage, in the case of a rabbinic sota her ḥalitza should not be effective to exempt her rival wife. And if you ask: Either way [mima nafshakh], it should be effective — for if she is considered like a full-fledged sota, her rival wife also does not require ḥalitza, and if she is not considered like a sota, then she rightly exempts her rival wife! [The answer is] that it is logical to the Gemara that since she resembles a biblical sota, her ḥalitza is as if it does not exist, and it should not exempt her rival wife.

Tosafot on Yevamot 11a:5:1.hebrew: מאן אחין אחין הנולדים - אומר ר"י דנולדים קרי לאותן העתידין להולד בלשון הש"ס, כדאמרינן בפרק ד' נדרים (נדרים ל:): "למימרא דנולדים העתידים משמע"; ובספ"ק דגיטין (דף יג: ושם) קאמר: "אלא מעתה הקנה לנולדים דלא הוו בשעת מתן מעות, ה"נ" כו':
Tosafot on Yevamot 11a:5:1.english: Who are the brothers? The brothers who are born [hanoladim] - R"i says that in the language of the Talmud, noladim refers to those who are destined to be born [in the future], as we say in the chapter Arba'ah Nedarim (Nedarim 30b): "Does this imply that noladim means those [who will be born in] the future?"; and at the end of the first chapter of Gittin (13b, and [see] there), it says: "But now, if one transferred [ownership] to noladim, who were not [yet in existence] at the time the money was given, so too," etc.:

Tosafot on Yevamot 11a:5:2.hebrew: צריכה חליצה מן האחין - מתייבמת אינה, מאחר דאסירה לבעלה; דהשתא במותר לה אסורה, באסור לה לא כ"ש:
Tosafot on Yevamot 11a:5:2.english: She requires ḥalitza from the brothers - She cannot enter into levirate marriage, since she was forbidden to her husband [who had previously performed ḥalitza with her]; for now, [if] she is forbidden to one who is [ordinarily] permitted to her, is she not all the more so [forbidden] to one who is forbidden to her?

Tosafot on Yevamot 11a:6:1.hebrew: כמאן כרבנן - הוה מצי לאוקומי כר"ש, כגון שנולד קודם שקדשה; אלא ניחא ליה לאוקמי כרבנן, ונולד אפילו אחר שקדשה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 11a:6:1.english: In accordance with whose [opinion]? In accordance with the Rabbis - [The Gemara] could have established [the case] in accordance with R. Shimon, such as where [the younger brother] was born before [the second brother] betrothed her; rather, it prefers to establish [it] in accordance with the Rabbis, [where] he was born even after he betrothed her.

Tosafot on Yevamot 11a:7:1.hebrew: חד אמר בעשה - כן גירסת הקונטרס, ופי' בקונטרס: משום דדרשינן "בית אחד הוא בונה ואינו בונה שתי בתים", ולאו הבא מכלל עשה — עשה. וקשה: כיון דאיצטריך קרא לגופיה, שלא ייבם את שתיהן, מנלן דאתיא קרא לנתקו מכלל כרת ללאו? ואמר ר"ת דגרסינן "חד אמר בלאו", וכן פר"ח, דכשייבם אחת קאי אצרה ב"לא יבנה", דקרינא בצרה: כיון שלא בנאה, שוב לא יבנה אותה; וכן האחים, לא קיימא עלה אלא בלאו לרבי יוחנן. וגרסינן שפיר: "וחזר ובא הוא או אחד מן האחין על צרתה". אבל לפ"ה דגרסינן "בעשה", לא פליגי אלא באחין, אבל איהו לכ"ע בעשה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 11a:7:1.english: One said: [In violation] of a positive commandment - This is the reading of Rashi, and Rashi explained [that it is] because we expound [the verse]: "One house he builds, and he does not build two houses," and a prohibition derived by implication from a positive commandment [has the status of] a positive commandment. And this is difficult: since the verse is needed for its own sake, [to teach] that he may not perform yibbum with both of them, from where do we [know] that the verse comes to remove it from the category of karet to a negative commandment? And Rabbeinu Tam said that we read: "One said: [In violation] of a negative commandment," and so too Rabbeinu Chananel explained: that when he performs yibbum with one [wife], he stands under [the prohibition of] "he shall not build" with respect to the rival wife, for we apply [the verse] to the rival wife: once he has not built her [house], he shall not build her again; and likewise [for] the brothers, she stands under nothing more than a negative commandment according to Rabbi Yochanan. And we properly read [in the Gemara]: "and subsequently he or one of the brothers had relations with her rival wife." However, according to Rashi's commentary, where we read "[in violation] of a positive commandment," they disagree only regarding the brothers, whereas he himself, according to everyone, [is in violation] of a positive commandment.

Tosafot on Yevamot 11a:9:1.hebrew: צרת סוטה אסורה - לאו דוקא "אסורה", דאף מחליצה פטורה, כדפירש בקונטרס. ודוקא סוטה ודאי, אבל סוטה ספק בעי חליצה, כדמייתי בסמוך. וקרא ד"ונסתרה והיא נטמאה" בנבעלה ודאי איירי, כדמסיק לקמן; אבל סוטה ספק לא כתב בה טומאה. וא"ת: והא תנן: "נכנסה עמו לבית הסתר — אסורה לביתה ואסורה לתרומה", ודרשינן בפרק כשם (סוטה דף כח. ושם): שלשה פעמים "ונטמאה" כתיב — אחד לבעל, ואחד לבועל, ואחד לתרומה! וי"ל: דלא אסרה הכתוב אלא משום ספק שמא נבעלה ונטמאה, ולעולם לא כתיב טומאה אלא על הודאי נבעלה. וא"ת: כיון שלא נכתב שם טומאה אלא על הודאי, אמאי אסורה לביתה ולתרומה? וי"ל: דעשה ספק כודאי, כדאמר בפרק כשם (ג"ז שם): "אם נטמאה למה שותה, ואם לא נטמאה למה נשקית? מגיד לך הכתוב שהספק אסורה כודאי". ולהכי ספק סוטה בעיא חליצה, דדוקא להחמיר עשה הכתוב ספק כודאי, ולא להקל לפטרה בלא חליצה. ולמאי דפרישית לעיל (יבמות דף ג: ד"ה לפי), דלמסקנא דשמעתין "טומאה כעריות כתיב בה" דאמר רב היינו במקום לאו — ניחא, דההוא טומאה לא כתיבא אלא על ודאי נבעלה. אבל מ"מ קשה: כיון דסוטה ודאי חשיב לה רב כערוה, א"כ סוטה ספק הוה לה ליחשב כספק ערוה, וא"כ היכי פריך "ותתייבם ייבומי":
Tosafot on Yevamot 11a:9:1.english: The rival wife of a sota is forbidden - [This does] not literally [mean merely] "forbidden," for she is even exempt from ḥalitza, as Rashi explained. And [this applies] specifically [to] a definite sota, whereas an uncertain sota requires ḥalitza, as [the Gemara] cites immediately below. And the verse, "and she was secluded and she was defiled" (Numbers 5:13), speaks of one who definitely had forbidden relations, as [the Gemara] concludes below; however, [regarding] an uncertain sota, "defilement" is not written about her. And if you ask: But we learned in a Mishnah: "[If] she entered with him into a secluded place, she is forbidden to her house [i.e., her husband] and forbidden to [eat] teruma," and we expound in chapter Keshem (Sotah 28a and elsewhere): Three times "and she was defiled" is written — one for the husband, one for the adulterer, and one for teruma! One can answer that Scripture only forbade her because of the uncertainty lest she had relations and was defiled, and in fact "defilement" is only written regarding one who definitely had relations. And if you ask: Since the term "defilement" is only written regarding the definite case, why is she forbidden to her house and to teruma? One can answer that [Scripture] treated an uncertain case like a definite case, as [the Gemara] says in chapter Keshem (ibid.): "If she was defiled, why does she drink [the bitter waters]? And if she was not defiled, why is she made to drink? Scripture tells you that the uncertain [sota] is forbidden like the definite [sota]." And therefore an uncertain sota requires ḥalitza, because Scripture only treated an uncertain case like a definite case to be stringent, and not to be lenient to exempt her without ḥalitza. And according to what I explained above (Yevamot 3b, s.v. Lefi), that according to the conclusion of our sugya, "defilement is written with regard to her as with forbidden relatives" which Rav stated means in place of a negative prohibition, [this] works well, since that "defilement" is only written regarding one who definitely had relations. Nevertheless, it is difficult: since Rav considers a definite sota like a forbidden relative, if so, an uncertain sota should be considered like an uncertain forbidden relative, and if so, how does [the Gemara] object: "And let her enter into levirate marriage"?
